about: Carisma Circle v2: the design of record's words (circle-spa-rollout-2026-11-17 src/kit.js CK.S and its parts, run on src/scenario.js) for every member state, with the BE-1 /client/loyalty/me body each state reads. Generated by gen_words.cjs; never edit by hand. A product copies this file into its own tests and proves its sentence builders say the same, byte for byte (ADDENDUM PART A X11). Fictional data (Maria Borg's week).

conventions.html: The kit's own HTML: <b> marks bold, & is an ampersand, '#terms' and '#join' stand for the product's own Terms and Join links.
conventions.text: The same words with the tags removed and the entities decoded; no-break spaces (U+00A0) and the curly apostrophe (U+2019) are kept. Compare text exactly.
conventions.null: The kit draws nothing for this key in this state.
conventions.brands: A key ending in [spa], [spa,aesthetics], [spa,slimming] or [spa,aesthetics,slimming] is that word with brands[] = houses[that key] (surfaces R5.2); every other key is the same for any brands[].
conventions.perks: Every /me body (perks, nextLevelPerks, levels[]) and status.levels[] says live {spaDays, earlyAccess, noDeposit} false each, BE-i's default: the (noPerksLive) keys are the words these bodies must give (the credit rate and the birthday credit only). The unsuffixed keys are the words with all three perks live: to prove them, set every live flag true in your copy of a body.
conventions.expiry: The /me expiry fields (pointsExpireAt, pointsExpireKind, datedEnds) are modelled for the dated lot only (her birthday credit); a state without one has null there, where BE-1 would send her balance's own lapse date. BE-1's `expiring` is left out (the scenario has no lapse date to give it). inputs.endingSoon is the kit's ending-soon state (S.expiring), not a BE-1 field: which API signal maps to it is for BE-1 and the product to decide.
conventions.designChecks: Places where kit.js's action contradicts the design's own rule (ADDENDUM A.0 X8), checked both ways on S.act(*), card.btn, card.btn(earned) and hero.btn: the words above stay the kit's; a product says `rule` there and skips exactly those keys until kit.js is fixed.
conventions.letters: Letters 04 (Back to booking: the level track, the earn line) and 08 (Recall: the Circle card) rewrite the kit's words as `letters.rewrites` says; compare those blocks after applying the same rewrites to the fixture's words. Letter 03 and every other surface use the words as they are.

letters.about: What letters 04 and 08 do to the kit's words, as their boards do it (circle-spa-rollout-2026-11-17/src/boards). Apply each rewrite with new RegExp(pattern, flags) and replacement to every key it names, in that letter only. Letter 08's Circle card action is also a text link, the design's action followed by ' ›', and the card has no action when her credit pays nothing (the letter's gold button is the booking).

designChecks.why: The kit withholds 'Use my credit' where her credit pays a treatment (affordable true); the design's rule is 'Use my credit' (ADDENDUM A.0 X8; CK.hero draws it for this same state; board 08, which draws this state, drops expiring before it calls CK.S.act, to get 'Use my credit'). kit.js S.act answers 'Book a visit' whenever the state carries expiring, whatever her credit pays.

The kit offers 'Use my credit' where her credit pays no treatment (affordable false); the design's rule is 'Book a visit' (ADDENDUM A.0 X8; CK.hero draws it for this same state). kit.js S.act never tests affordability: it says 'Book a visit' only for expiring, a €0 balance or a first-reward gap (m.first), and this state has none of them.
